Adopt Me
uh-DOPT mee
proper noun (Gen Alpha slang)
Adopt Me!, a Roblox role-play game released in July 2017 by the studio later called Uplift Games. Players began as parents or babies adopting one another, then — from 2019 — as collectors adopting, raising, and trading pets hatched from eggs: dogs, unicorns, dragons, "neon" and "mega neon" versions made by combining four of the same pet. It drew more than a million players at once at its 2019–20 peak, and its pet-trading economy, with "legendary" pets valued like baseball cards, taught a generation the words trade, value, W or L, and scammer.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To a Gen Alpha child, Adopt Me is the Roblox game about raising pets and trading them, and "What’s your best pet in Adopt Me?" is a question about wealth. Kids spend hours caring for virtual pets, and more hours haggling over their value. The Christian observation: the game’s very name borrows one of the most beautiful words in the New Testament. Adoption is how God brings sinners into His family: "ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15). God "predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself" (Eph 1:5) — not because we were the rare, valuable pet, but because He loved us. The game’s habit runs the other way: a pet is loved for what it is worth in trade, and a better one is always on offer. That is the very thing God’s adoption is not. He does not trade His children up. "When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up" (Psa 27:10). A father can tell a five-year-old: "In the game, people adopt pets and trade them for better ones. God adopted you, and He will never, ever trade you for anybody." And the nurturing play is worth praising: "A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast" (Pro 12:10).

Webster 1828 Definition

Roblox pet-raising and trading game (2017; pets from 2019) whose name borrows the gospel’s word for God’s family — a chance to teach the adoption that is never traded.

expand to see more

ADOPT ME, proper n. (Roblox game, 2017–present; Gen Alpha usage) The pet-adopting, pet-raising, pet-trading role-play game. "I got a mega neon in Adopt Me!"

Vocabulary it spread: neon / mega neon (upgraded pets), legendary, trade value, W or L? (was that trade a win or loss?).

Decode for parents: the caring play is sweet; the trading economy is where scams, envy, and real-money side markets live.

Webster 1828, the root — ADOPT, v.t. To take a stranger into one’s family, as son and heir; to take one who is not a child, and treat him as one, giving him a title to the privileges and rights of a child.

Key Scripture

Rom 8:15 — "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father."

Eph 1:5 — "Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,"

Psa 27:10 — "When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up."

Pro 12:10 — "A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel."

Gal 4:5 — "To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons."

Modern Corruption

Adopt Me borrows the gospel’s tenderest word and turns it into a market where every pet is loved for its trade value; God’s adoption is the opposite — unearned, unpriced, never traded.

expand to see more

The game’s double life is the lesson. Children do care for their pets, feeding and bathing them, and that nurture is good. But the economy rewards only rarity, so the beloved pet becomes an asset, and the trading screen becomes a school of envy and haggling. A child can learn there to measure love by market value.

Christ redeemed "them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons" (Gal 4:5). That adoption is a costly act of love toward the unworthy, sealed with blood, never revisited. Tell your child often that he is adopted into God’s family by grace, and that God’s children are not traded up. A game named Adopt Me can become a bedtime talk about Romans 8.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin adoptare (to choose for oneself) → English adopt → Adopt Me! (Roblox, 2017; pets 2019) → Gen Alpha’s pet-trading economy.

expand to see more

Latin ad + optare, to choose — to take a child as one’s own

Greek huiothesia — "placing as a son," Paul’s word for adoption (Rom 8:15; Eph 1:5)

July 2017: Adopt Me! released on Roblox as a family role-play

2019: pets and eggs added; neon and mega neon combining

2019–20: more than a million concurrent players; a trading economy with its own slang

Usage

""Would you trade your frost dragon for my shadow dragon? W or L?""

"In the game a pet is traded up; in the gospel the adopted child never is (Rom 8:15)."

"A righteous child regardeth the life of her beast — even a pixel puppy (Pro 12:10)."
